passages.english: And to Timothy he says, "For when they have grown wanton in Christ, they wish to marry" (1 Tim. 5:11); and elsewhere, "But also all who wish to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution" (2 Tim. 3:12); and to Timothy himself, "Do not neglect the grace that is in you" (1 Tim. 4:14). And to Philemon: "So that your good [deed] might not be as if of necessity, but of [your own] will" (Philem. 14). He also admonishes slaves themselves to serve their masters from the heart with good will (Eph. 6:6). passages.notes: Many scanning errors silently corrected (e.g. 'deticiis' for 'deliciis', 'Noti' for 'Noli', 'eat' for 'est', 'tuam velat' for 'tuum veluti', 'ctiam' for 'etiam', 'hem' for 'Item', 'voluntale' for 'voluntate'). 'In deliciis egerint' (Vulgate 'luxuriatae fuerint') rendered 'grown wanton'. The passage breaks off mid-reference; the citation (James 4:11) continues in the following text.

passages.original: hoc autem ut caveantur, sive vincantur : quod a Patre qui in caelis est, nulla ratione peteremus, si virtute voluntatis humane hoc possemus efficcre. Commoneo autcm Charitatem vestram, et multum exhortor, ut hemi Cypriani librum quetn scripsit de Oratione Dominica, diligenter legatis; et quantum vos Dominus adjuverit, intelligatis, memoriæque mandetis. Ibi videbitis quemadmodum sic alloquatur liberum arbitrium eorum, quos conscriptione sui sermonis aedittcat, ut ostendat tamen ca quac implenda jubentur1 in lege, in oratione esse poscenda.
passages.english: but this [we say] so that they may be avoided or overcome; and we would by no means ask this from the Father who is in heaven if we could bring it about by the strength of the human will. I remind your Charity, and strongly urge you, to read carefully the book of the blessed Cyprian which he wrote on the Lord's Prayer, and, as far as the Lord helps you, to understand it and commit it to memory. There you will see how he addresses the free will of those whom he edifies by the writing of his discourse in such a way as nevertheless to show that the things which are commanded in the law to be fulfilled must be asked for in prayer.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected: 'efficcre' for 'efficere', 'autcm' for 'autem', 'hemi' for 'beati' (blessed), 'quetn' for 'quem', 'aedittcat' for 'aedificat', 'ca quac' for 'ea quae'. The '1' after 'jubentur' is a footnote mark and has been omitted.
